newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Pequiven profits rise despite recession.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Pequiven profits rise despite recession.

text.p: Pequiven, the petrochemical subsidiary of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela, said 1996 post- tax profits jumped 134 percent to $206 million despite a domestic recession and lower world prices, the company said Wednesday.

Sales fell by $10 million to $760 million, but higher production levels and more efficient financial and manufacturing processes had more than outweighed the fall, said Pequiven president Arnold Volkenborn.
"World chemicals prices were low in 1996 compared to 1995... nevertheless, Pequiven managed to increase its profits," he told journalists on Wednesday.

The price of ethylene, urea and methanol fell by 21, 9 and 37 percent respectively in 1996, but Pequiven's production rose by 300,000 tonnes to 4.4 million tonnes. And Volkenborn expected prices in 1997 to be slightly higher than last year.
Contributions from associated companies almost doubled to $45 million in 1996, against $23 million the year before.

Volkenborn said he hoped Venezuela's Congress would approve a law leading to the privatisation of Pequiven by the end of the current session of Congress in July this year, adding that he would favour flotation of more than 50 percent of the company.
He said privatisation was necessary to raise the capital needed for Pequiven's ambitious growth strategy.

Volkenborn highlighted a $1.6 billion joint-venture signed with Mobil Chemical Corp for a new olefin and plastics plant at Jose on the Caribbean coast. This plant is expected come on stream in 2000 with annual production of 830,000 tonnes of ethylene, 480,000 tonnes of polyethylene and 430,000 tonnes of glycol.
But he said a previously planned $700 million joint-venture with Arcadian Corporation fell through after Arcadian was acquired by Potash Corp.
